When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **84** (strong buy, capitulation) vs Macro regime CONTRACTION **70%** and risk off bias with **3** signals aligned
One gauge says sentiment is washed out and the other says the economy is weakening. Trust the regime for sizing and the contrarian score for timing, because capitulation can last weeks inside a contraction.

The broad average looks quiet while the sharpest pairs have already broken their old relationships. Trust the jaws score, since averages hide concentrated breaks in semis, momentum and regional banks.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **2/10** (monitoring only) vs VIX Spike tier **1/4** with skew active and **50%** spike probability

Bear

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The call is cautious patience. Sentiment is stretched to the downside (contrarian score 84), but the macro regime reads CONTRACTION at 70% confidence and the regime score of 55 sits in a transition band with 3 risk off signals lined up. Price damage is limited so far, with the Crash Index at only 2/10.

The tension sits between those two readings. Fear this deep usually pays a buyer who waits, yet contraction regimes punish early entries. The VIX Spike Detector shows tier 1/4 with a 50% spike probability and skew active, which means options traders already pay for downside protection while backwardation stays off. You get a market that is nervous but not in panic. That favors staged buying in small tranches and keeping dry powder, because a full size entry needs the confluence signals to fire first.

The main risk is the divergence picture. The mother jaws score is 100, and 6 pairs have broken their long run relationships, including semis against the S&P 500 and momentum against the S&P 500. If the Nasdaq 100 (-4.4% over 5 days) keeps leading lower, the contraction call gets confirmed. The reading that flips the stance is VIX backwardation turning on: it moves the posture from patient to defensive within one session.

AI read · macro regime

In a contraction you favor quality balance sheets, shorter duration risk and smaller position sizes than the contrarian score of 84 would suggest by itself. Stocks and bonds have decoupled (correlation drift from +0.75 to -0.22), so Treasuries can work as a hedge again.

Add exposure in thirds and let the regime score confirm before the last tranche. A regime reading that drops under confirmation, or a contrarian score that fades without a price bounce, would tell you the contraction is deepening.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together have started to move apart. Correlation drift is the measured change in how tightly they move together, shown here as old reading to new reading.

The composite zone is CALM, with 16 of 43 pairs (37.2%) diverging and a net bias of -4 (6 bearish against 10 bullish). The mother jaws score of 100 says the sharpest breaks are extreme anyway.

Semis against the S&P 500 fell from +0.89 to -0.16, so chips no longer lead the index. Momentum against the S&P 500 went from +0.83 to -0.35, so winners have stopped pulling the market.

Regional banks against financials dropped from +0.41 to -0.65, which flags stress in smaller lenders. Stocks against bonds moved from +0.75 to -0.22, so bonds are acting like a hedge again.

The yield curve pair went from -0.51 to +0.33, and AUD/JPY from +0.57 to -0.36. When leaders and followers split like this, indexes often hold while the internals crack.

Watch semis and regional banks first.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Leadership is scattered, and that points to rotation. In Asia, the KOSPI (^KS11) leads at +3.6% over 5 days while Shanghai (000001.SS) lags at -2.5%.

In Europe, the DAX (^GDAXI) leads at +2.5% and the FTSE (^FTSE) trails at +0.4%. In the US, the Russell 2000 (^RUT) leads at +0.7% while the Nasdaq 100 (^NDX) lags at -4.4%.

Crypto trades down, with Ethereum at -4.3% and Solana at -9.7%. Money is leaving large tech and speculative risk and landing in small caps and the DAX.

For today's US session, expect pressure on mega cap tech to continue and relative support for small caps. A weak crypto bid overnight would add to the risk off tone.

A Nasdaq 100 rebound that outpaces the Russell 2000 would end the rotation and ease the bear case.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 2/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index sits at 2/10, which means only 1 or 2 classic stress signals are lit, so price action is calm. The VIX Spike Detector reads tier 1/4 (BROAD) with a 50% spike probability and skew active.

Skew is the extra price traders pay for downside puts over upside calls, so it shows hedging demand before any price damage. Backwardation is off, meaning near term fear still trades below longer dated fear.

Both readings are coherent: the market has not fallen yet, but buyers of protection are early. Today that gap is small, and tier 1 is the lowest alert step.

A move to backwardation, or a Crash Index rise toward 4/10, would turn the calm into a warning. Until then, treat the 50% spike odds as a reason to hold hedges, not to add risk.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 2/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

How to read
Aggregation of all panel signals across the 4 cross-asset buckets. RISK-ON = risk appetite (cyclical, equity, EM). RISK-OFF = flight to defensives (TLT, gold, JPY). STRESS = liquidity tension (HYG, MOVE, STLFSI). TOPPING = end-of-cycle signals (concentration, breadth narrowing, defensives leading). Doctrine: a single signal = noise. 3+ aligned in one bucket = real confirmed regime.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
